notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2024, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Debt service leaves out $1,469,000 of principal repaid with new borrowing the county did not spend on capital that year, most likely refinancing or a rolled-over note.
Payments to other governments ($6,958,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money counts contributions from businesses, unions and PACs to county board and county office candidates, reported to the State Board of Elections since 2023. Illinois allows business contributions. Individuals, candidates' own money, party and candidate committees, loans and other receipts are not counted.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Illinois yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: License-plate readers
redFlags.detail: The Winnebago County Sheriff's Office operates 44 Flock Safety automated license plate readers as of September 2025.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS017382, citing Public Records From the EFF via Pittsboro Police - See note

redFlags.label: Police drones
redFlags.detail: The Winnebago County Sheriff's Office has nine drones, according to the 2024 Illinois Freedom from Drone Surveillance Act Report. The agency conducted 13 drone flights between July 2023 and March 2024.
